Definition: properly, to entwine as a screen; by implication, to fence in, cover over, (figuratively) protect
BiblicalUsage: The Old Testament word çâkak means to entwine as a screen, to fence in, to cover over and protect. It appears 24 times, and the passages that use it — 1 Chronicles and 1 Kings among them — show it in its natural setting. Read them together and the meaning settles itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God chose çâkak on purpose. To entwine as a screen, to fence in, to cover over and protect is not an accident of language; it is the way He says what He means.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
